Below is a single, comprehensive build prompt that specifies the entire system end‑to‑end, derived from a full line‑by‑line reading of the provided source. It is written as a standalone instruction set ready to hand to any model or developer to implement the complete, production‑ready application with no omissions.[1]

 Comprehensive Build Prompt

Build a complete, productionready, mobilefirst AI chat web application consisting of a singlepage frontend (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, no build step required) and a backend HTTP API that streams AI responses over ServerSent Events (SSE). Deliver full, unabridged, working source code for every file — no placeholders, no mock data, no simplified standins. The application must run standalone in a browser and communicate with the backend exclusively through the API contract defined below.

 Global Page Structure and Metadata

Create an HTML document with lang="hu" (Hungarian) as the primary UI language. Include full responsive viewport meta tags (width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover, interactive-widget=resizes-content), PWA metadata (mobile-web-app-capable, apple-mobile-web-app-capable, apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style=black-translucent, apple-mobile-web-app-title, application-name), dual light/dark theme-color meta tags, color-scheme set to dark light, and format-detection=telephone=no. Reference a web app manifest and a full icon set (180, 152, 167, 192 px Apple touch icons plus a generated inline SVG favicon using a roundedsquare appicon glyph). Load a syntaxhighlighting library and its stylesheet (dark theme) for code block rendering inside AI responses.

 Visual Design System

Implement a CSS customproperty based theming system supporting both dark and light modes via prefers-color-scheme. Define variables for foreground text at three opacities, background color, separator color, hover overlay, and a set of "liquid glass" tokens (semitransparent gradient layers, border colors, inset highlights, shadow colors, an accent blue/indigo hue, and a sendbutton glow color). Build a reusable .lg "liquid glass" utility class that gives any panel a frostedglass look: a layered gradient background, a hairline border, multilayer inset/outset boxshadows, backdrop-filter: blur(36px) saturate(190%) contrast(1.08) brightness(1.04) (with -webkit- prefix), an isolated stacking context, and two pseudoelements (::before for a soft diagonal highlight using mix-blend-mode: screen, ::after for a subtle inner border glow). All interactive surfaces (sidebar, message input bar, history cards, searchresult chip bar) must use this glass treatment.

Disable text selection and native touch callouts globally except inside chat bubbles, markdown content, code blocks, and form fields, where text selection must be explicitly reenabled. Disable doubletap zoom and touch highlight color on all buttons, links, labels, and icons. Use -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "SF Pro Display", "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif as the font stack, with antialiased/legible text rendering.

Render an animated fullviewport background behind the app: a fixed #bg layer with a diagonal linear gradient tinted blue/indigo/black at low opacity and heavy blur, plus a second pseudolayer darkening the composition with a vertical gradient overlay, each with distinct lightmode variants (softer pastel gradients, lighter overlays).

 WebGL Glass Refraction Renderer

Implement an optional WebGL2based realtime "glass" rendering effect layered as a fullscreen canvas (#glass-renderer-canvas). It must gracefully noop if WebGL2 or the EXT_color_buffer_float extension is unavailable. Implement it as a multipass renderer:

1. A vertex shader producing a fullscreen triangle without a vertex buffer (using gl_VertexID).
2. A background fragment shader that procedurally renders a slowly animated, paletteshifting radialblob gradient as the base scene, driven by a time uniform.
3. A separable Gaussian blur fragment shader with a configurable kernel (support kernel radius up to 200, computed via a Gaussian weight function normalized so weights sum to 1), applied first horizontally then vertically to produce a blurred version of the background.
4. A "main" composite fragment shader that: defines any number of roundedrectangle glass shapes (up to 48) via signeddistancefield roundedrect functions; computes surface normals of the SDF via finite differences; computes an edge band where the fragment is near the shape boundary; refracts the blurred background texture inside each shape based on the normal direction and a configurable thickness/refractionfactor/dispersion (chromatic aberration by offsetting R, G, B sample points differently); computes a Fresnelstyle rim highlight and a directional specular glare band (configurable angle, convergence, hardness, and factor); blends background, refracted/blurred glass, Fresnel highlight, and glare into a final color; and supports numbered debugoutput "steps" (distance field, normals, edge mask, blurred texture, refractiononly, Fresnelonly, glareonly, insidemask, backgroundonly) selectable via a step uniform for development inspection.

Manage two pingponged halffloat RGBA16F framebuffers plus a background framebuffer, all resized on window resize/DPR change (clamp device pixel ratio to a maximum of 2). Recompute the Gaussian kernel weights whenever the blur radius changes. Expose a single configuration object with tunable parameters: edge thickness, refraction factor, dispersion amount, Fresnel range/hardness/factor, glare range/hardness/factor/convergence/oppositefactor/angle, RGBA tint with alpha, background type, shape width/height/corner radius/roundness, shapemerge rate, and blur radius, plus an animation "step" flag for the render loop.

 Application Shell Layout

Structure the app as a fixedheight (100dvh) flex column #app containing: a slidein left #sidebar (fixed position, 300px wide, max 85% viewport width, translated offscreen by default, animated in with a springlike cubicbezier transition, backed by a semitransparent blurred panel), a fullscreen dimmed .sb-backdrop overlay that fades in/out with the sidebar and closes it on tap, a scrollable #content region containing #scroll-area and #msg-list, and a fixed bottom #ib-wrap input bar that respects safearea insets on all four edges (env(safe-area-inset-*)).

 Sidebar (Conversation History Panel)

Header row (.sb-hdr, 52px tall) with a centered title, a searchtoggle icon button, and a close button (both circular, scaledown active states). Below the header, an expandable/collapsible search bar (#sb-search-bar) that animates open/closed via height and visibility transitions, containing a rounded search input with a leading magnifier icon and a "Cancel" text button that appears only while the search bar is open.

Below that, a scrollable .sb-body containing: a "New Chat" glass button (icon + label) that clears the current conversation and its session id; section labels for grouping conversations (e.g., pinned vs. by recency); and a list (#hlist) of history cards (.hcard). Each card shows a singleline, ellipsistruncated preview of the first user message (support inline <mark> highlighting of searchmatched substrings), a small metadata line (relative timestamp), a delete iconbutton that is always visible on touch devices and only visible on hover/focus for pointer devices, and an optional pin indicator icon shown only when the conversation is pinned. Cards must support: single tap to switch conversation, tap on the delete icon to remove that conversation (client list update plus a DELETE /api/history?session_id=... backend call, no confirmation dialog blocking the UI), a longpress (500ms on touch, or rightclick/contextmenu on desktop) that opens a contextual action sheet for a card (rename, pin/unpin, delete), and inline rename via making the title contenteditable. Show an emptystate illustration (icon + explanatory paragraph) when there is no history.

Sidebar interactions must support a dragtoclose gesture (tracking touch/pointer movement while dragging class disables the CSS transition, then reenabling the transition and snapping open/closed based on drag distance/velocity), plus a "pull hint" affordance shown near the top while dragging past a threshold.

Persist the full history list to localStorage, including perconversation id, title/preview text, pinned flag, and lastupdated timestamp; maintain an inmemory Map from session id to array index for O(1) lookups, and resort with pinned conversations first, then mostrecentfirst, on every mutation.

 Main Chat Area

Render messages grouped by consecutive samerole turns inside .msg-group (aligned right for user, class="u"; aligned left for assistant, class="a"). User messages render inside a .bubble with a colored gradient background, border, glass blur, and rounded corners (max 85% width). Assistant messages render as .ai-bubble with transparent background and no border/shadow (full width), so they read like plain body text rather than a chat bubble. Both bubble types must support inline attached images rendered as rounded thumbnails (.img-in-msg) capped at 220×185px with object-fit: cover.

Implement a full Markdown renderer (paragraphs, headings h1–h3, ordered/unordered lists, links opening in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer", horizontal rules, inline code spans styled as pillshaped monospace tags, and fenced code blocks). Fenced code blocks must be syntaxhighlighted using the loaded highlighting library, matched by language identifier, and rendered inside a <pre><code> structure with copytoclipboard affordance.

Below every completed assistant message, render an action row (.t-row) with icontext buttons (.tact) for at least "copy" (copies the raw content to the clipboard) and "retry" (resends the last user turn and regenerates the response) plus a timestamp label (.btime). Show a threedot bouncing "typing" indicator (.typing with .td dots, staggered animation delays) while waiting for the first token of a new response, and remove it as soon as content starts streaming in.

Support inline live "web/agent search" progress inside an assistant message while it is being generated: on a search_start event render a .srch-wrap block with a spinning magnifier icon and the literal search query text (label the block "Keresés: <query>" — Hungarian for "Search: <query>"); on sources/search_results events, populate a horizontally scrollable chip list where each chip is a link showing a favicon (fetched via a favicon service keyed by domain) and the bare hostname (strip leading www.), and update a resultcount label (Hungarian "N forrás" — "N sources"); on search_done, visually mark the search bar as complete (e.g., stop the spinner, add a "done" class).

On any error or warning streaming event, render a distinct inline error bubble (.err-bbl) with a translucent tinted background instead of throwing or silently failing.

If a stream disconnects and is being retried automatically, show a persistent reconnect banner (.rcn-bar) with a spinning icon and status text; implement exponential backoff for reconnect attempts (base delay 1500ms, multiplier 1.8, capped at 30000ms) and cancel/clear the banner once a retry succeeds.

 Message Input Bar

Fixed to the bottom of the viewport, containing (top to bottom): an optional horizontally scrollable strip of attachedimage thumbnails (.img-strip, each thumb 50×50px rounded, with a small circular remove button .img-rm overlaid topright), then an input row (.ib-row) with: a circular attach/imagepicker icon button, an autogrowing multiline text input (contenteditable or <textarea>, growing up to a max height of ~176px, no visible scrollbar, placeholder text, 16px font to avoid iOS zoomonfocus), and a circular send button with a colored glass gradient background that is disabled (dimmed, noninteractive) whenever the input is empty and no images are attached, and that morphs into a stop/cancel control while a response is streaming.

Pressing send (or hitting Enter without Shift) must: build a payload containing the user's text, any attached images (base64 data URLs or uploaded references), the current session id (or null for a new conversation), and the selected mode/model if applicable; immediately render the user's message bubble and clear the input and attachment strip; then open the streaming request.

 Streaming Protocol (Frontend Consumption)

Implement a fetchbased POST to the chatsend endpoint with an AbortController for cancellation, reading the response body as a stream via res.body.getReader(), decoding UTF8 chunks incrementally, and parsing them as newlinedelimited SSE frames (event: <type>\ndata: <json>\n\n) via an incremental buffer parser that only consumes complete frames and retains partial trailing data for the next chunk. Dispatch parsed events to a single handler switching on event type:

 session: capture/update the current session id (sid/session_id field) and persist/rerender history.
 content: append the delta/text/content field to a growing buffer, cap the buffer at 256,000 characters (drop oldest), and schedule a throttled rerender via requestAnimationFrame with a minimum 70ms interval between DOM updates (rerun Markdown rendering and set innerHTML on the message's content node) — never rerender on every single delta to avoid layout thrashing.
 search_start, sources/search_results, search_done: render the inline search UI described above.
 error/warning: render the inline error bubble.
 done: mark the stream finished and clear any persisted "active job" marker from localStorage.

On stream completion, push the assembled assistant message into the inmemory message array, attach copy/retry action buttons, persist updated history metadata, and autoscroll to bottom if the user was already near the bottom (do not forcescroll if the user has manually scrolled up to read earlier content). On network/stream failure that is not a deliberate user abort, apply the autoretrywithbackoff behavior above; on deliberate abort, if partial content was already received, save it as the final assistant message rather than discarding it.

 Job Persistence and ResumeAfterReload

Whenever a send begins, immediately write {job_id, sid, mode} to localStorage under a fixed key. On every app load, check for a stored active job: query a jobstatus endpoint; if the job is still running, reconstruct a fresh chat view for that session and reconnect to a resumestreaming endpoint that replays/continues the SSE event stream from where it left off; if the job finished while the tab was closed, clear the stored marker and, if the finished session differs from the currently displayed one, load that session's persisted history instead. Additionally, on load, if there is a currently open session id but no stored job marker, poll a persession "active job" endpoint to catch jobs that were started from another tab/device.

 Conversation Session Management

Maintain: an inmemory array of message objects {role, content, ts, imageUrls?} for the active conversation; a sid variable holding the current backend session id (null for an unsaved new conversation); functions to start a new chat (abort any active stream, clear the message list DOM and array, optionally clear the session id, clear attachments, reset the input box height); a function to load a conversation by id that fetches its full message history from the backend, rebuilds the DOM (rendering both user and assistant messages, restoring any attached images from either raw URLs or a payloadtodataURL conversion helper), applies any locallytracked "deleted message" overrides, and scrolls to the bottom; and a function to switch between conversations that guards against reloading the alreadyactive session. Use monotonically increasing generation counters to guard every async load/stream operation against race conditions from rapid conversation switching (a completed async operation must check it is still the "current" generation before mutating the DOM).

 Backend API Contract

Implement a backend service (any modern server framework) exposing:

 A chatsend endpoint (POST) accepting the message payload (text, optional images, session id or null, mode) and responding with a text/event-stream SSE stream emitting the event types listed above (session, content, search_start, sources/search_results, search_done, error, warning, done) as they occur, ultimately persisting the full exchange (user message + assistant message, including any websearch sources used) to durable storage keyed by session id.
 GET /api/history?session_id=<id> returning either a bare array of {role, content, images?, ts} messages or an object with a messages array, representing the full ordered message history for that session.
 DELETE /api/history?session_id=<id> permanently deleting that conversation's stored history.
 GET /api/job/<job_id>/status returning {status: "running"|"done", session_id}.
 GET /api/session/<session_id>/active_job returning {status, job_id, session_id} describing whether a job is currently running for that session.
 GET /api/agent/resume/<job_id> returning a text/event-stream that replays/continues the SSE events for an inprogress job so a reconnecting client can resume exactly where a previous connection left off.

All endpoints must handle malformed/missing parameters with proper HTTP status codes and JSON error bodies, must not crash the server process on invalid input, and must be backed by real persistent storage (a real database or durable filebacked store) — no inmemoryonly mock persistence, since history must survive server restarts.

 NonNegotiable Implementation Requirements

Deliver the complete frontend as real, functioning HTML/CSS/JavaScript (not abbreviated snippets) and the complete backend as real, functioning server code implementing every endpoint above with genuine streaming, genuine persistence, and genuine session/job tracking. Every interactive behavior described above (sidebar drag/search/pin/delete/rename, streaming with throttled Markdown rerender, inline search progress chips, autoretry with backoff, job resume after reload, image attachment and removal, glass visual effects) must be fully implemented and working endtoend, with no stubbed handlers, no "TODO" placeholders, and no simulated/fake API responses.

 search_start, sources/search_results, search_done: render the inline search UI described above, if the endpoint emits these event types.
 error/warning: render the inline error bubble.
 done: mark the stream finished.

On stream completion, push the assembled assistant message into the inmemory message array, attach copy/retry action buttons, persist the full updated conversation (including the new turn) to localStorage, and autoscroll to bottom if the user was already near the bottom (do not forcescroll if the user has manually scrolled up to read earlier content). On network/stream failure that is not a deliberate user abort, apply the autoretrywithbackoff behavior above; on deliberate abort, if partial content was already received, save it as the final assistant message rather than discarding it.

Expose a simple settings mechanism (a small settings panel or localStoragebacked configuration) where the API endpoint URL, API key/token, and model identifier can be entered and stored clientside, and used as headers/body fields on every outgoing request; never hardcode secrets into the shipped source.

 Conversation Session Management (ClientSide Only)

Maintain: an inmemory array of message objects {role, content, ts, imageUrls?} for the active conversation; a sid variable holding the current local conversation id (null for an unsaved new conversation, generated clientside once the first message is sent); functions to start a new chat (abort any active stream, clear the message list DOM and array, clear the session id, clear attachments, reset the input box height); a function to load a conversation by id that reads its full message history from localStorage, rebuilds the DOM (rendering both user and assistant messages, restoring attached images from stored data URLs), and scrolls to the bottom; and a function to switch between conversations that guards against reloading the alreadyactive session. Use monotonically increasing generation counters to guard every async load/stream operation against race conditions from rapid conversation switching (a completed async operation must check it is still the "current" generation before mutating the DOM).

 NonNegotiable Implementation Requirements

Deliver the complete application as real, functioning HTML/CSS/JavaScript (not abbreviated snippets), containing zero backend/server code, zero serverside endpoints, and zero serverside persistence — every piece of state (conversation history, settings, attachments) must be stored and managed entirely in the browser. Every interactive behavior described above (sidebar drag/search/pin/delete/rename, streaming with throttled Markdown rerender, inline search progress chips, autoretry with backoff, image/file attachment and removal, glass visual effects) must be fully implemented and working endtoend, with no stubbed handlers, no "TODO" placeholders, and no simulated/fake responses — the only external call permitted is the direct clienttoAPI streaming request described above.
